/SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Issued at 300 AM EDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Sunday - Tuesday Night...

Heat and humidity take a notable jump on Sunday as the strong 
western and central CONUS ridge becomes more established to our 
west. Expecting afternoon highs to peak in the upper 80s to around 
90 across the area, along with a notable jump in surface dewpoints 
to the low and mid 70s for most. The resulting max heat indices are 
expected to reach into the 95 to 100 degree range for some locations 
mainly along and west of I-65. Could take some folks off guard given 
the recent pleasant stretch of T/Tds we just had.

NW flow will continue over our region on the eastern periphery of 
the upper ridge, however Sunday looks to be mostly void of any 
notable triggering features. The lack of a trigger combined with 
some capping between H85-H7 on soundings suggest we'll stay mostly 
dry through the day. This notion is backed up by current model data, 
and it is a good thing as we will be strongly unstable (3000-4000 
J/KG of ML/SB CAPE).

The bigger storm concern focuses on later Sunday night through 
Monday night, and possibly again on Tuesday. Forecast data has been 
fairly consistent in suggesting that a convective complex or two 
could develop upstream and move through the NW flow pattern sometime 
in the Monday/Tuesday timeframe, although it has been inconsistent 
run to run with timing/placement, etc. It does appear that a series 
of shortwaves embedded within the NW flow aloft will trigger 
complexes up toward the western Great Lakes, and then ride SE on the 
NW flow pattern. Still don't have a lot of confidence on whether 
these complexes will impact our CWA or stay to the NE. Past 
experience has shown that a combination of 700-300mb mean wind 
combined with instability gradients can be a good way to determine 
cold pool driven MCS paths. Looks like we could easily have 4000+ 
J/KG of SB CAPE available across the entire Ohio River Valley region 
by Monday, however the sharp gradient evident on Sunday will be more 
broad and not well defined by Monday. As a result, expect the 700-
300 mb mean wind to be more of the driver of any cold pool driven 
forward propagating MCS in this particular scenario. This probably 
makes the more likely scenario that the bulk of MCS activity stays 
to our north and east, and only brings western portions of any 
convective complexes into play for us. That being said, a widespread 
damaging wind event is still a scenario that could occur and it 
still looks most likely across the NE half of the CWA sometime 
Monday-Tuesday.

Will have to keep our guard up and monitor hi-res CAM guidance over 
the next 48 hours as a severe threat will come into play if any of 
the convective complexes do end up impacting our area. Strong 
instability combined with plenty of deep layer shear (mainly driven 
by mid and upper level jet dynamics) would be capable of producing a 
wind damage threat, perhaps widespread wind damage if a good cold 
pool does get going upstream and forward propagates into our area. 
Like the addition of our area to the SPC Outlooks as it is kinda of 
an all or nothing type of scenario to message. Just keep in mind 
that it is conditional. 

If we do stay mostly dry into the early part of the week then the 
big story will end up being the heat and humidity. Talking about 
this 2nd since it is dependent on a convectively reinforced cold 
pool not diving in here and wrecking the temperature forecast. The 
current forecast calls for highs in the lower 90s both Monday and 
Tuesday. These values combined with dew points surging into the low 
and mid 70s could yield max heat indices up around 105 in some spots 
each afternoon. This would mainly be for area along and west of I-
65, and may need a Heat Advisory to cover this assuming we are able 
to stay more dry than not.

Wednesday - Friday...

NW flow aloft continues to persist over our area through mid to late 
week between the central/western CONUS ridge and the New England 
troughing. There is decent model agreement that we stay mostly dry 
during this time as the NW flow aloft doesn't look to harbor any 
embedded shortwaves. Still a bit early to be too confident, but for 
now it looks like the heat and humidity also back off a bit during 
this time. Highs look more around normal and mostly in the upper 80s 
during this stretch.
